The change itself is one line, but it lands on a published contract. `routes/users.js:6` emits `userId`, and the README states:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

**Consequence:** renaming `userId` → `user_id` in place breaks all three consumers on deploy. The iOS app is the sharp edge — shipped 3.2+ clients can't be updated in lockstep, so they'd read `undefined` until users upgrade. The nightly partner export is likely to fail silently until someone notices bad data. This is exactly the case the README says goes through a versioned endpoint.
